### **Job Description and Duties**


**Per CCR 249\.3, this job control may be used to fill subsequent vacancies.**  

**This is a 12\-month Limited Term (LT) position that may be extended up to 24 months or may become permanent.**  

Under the supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the incumbent performs a broad range of scientific and professional office and field duties involving the research, environmental analysis, outreach, and logistics for the Biological Control Program and the Integrated Pest Control Branch.  

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food \& Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!  

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. The CDFA does not participate in E\-Verify for employment authorization purposes.
You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


Approximately 60% of the workload will be in permanent buildings or trailers leased or owned by the State or cooperating agencies or other locations. The setting is standard with a phone, computer, keyboard, desks, tables, chairs, fax machine, copier, stapler, printers, calculators, and writing instruments. Computer software used may include MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access, and Publisher as well as other databases/software created especially for a given research task.  

The remaining 40% of the workload requires traveling to remote and/or populated areas within the State of California via government (State or Federal) vehicle (car/truck). Incumbent will be required to travel. Travel may be on a short notice that requires full days or few to several nights in length.  

When working in the field, the incumbent works alone or with a group of field scientists and/or seasonals. Incumbent works with varied and unfamiliar vehicles and equipment, including excavators, airboats, kayaks, trailers, pumps of various kinds, and ATVs. The incumbent may work in isolated locations and may work alone for extended periods. Often, activities may require driving for several hours (alone or with company), lifting objects, and moving equipment of various weights. Also, the incumbent may encounter extremes in temperature, humidity, variable terrain (smooth to irregular and unstable), and often aquatic or riparian situations. Incumbent may be required to enter or swim in bodies of water (lakes and ponds) that vary in temperature, length, width, and depth. Incumbent may also be required to navigate variable lengths of distance over unpredictable terrain. Various sitting, bending, stooping, standing, and reaching motions may be required on an irregular basis. Noise level for work is variable.  

Incumbent may work extended hours and days at any given time in the month including holidays. The incumbent may be required on short notice to work on emergency projects for the Branch or any other program for the Plant Division. The work environment for these projects closely resembles the above and may involve a longer travel day.  

This position may/may not be eligible for telework. The amount of telework is at the discretion of the CDFA and based on the current telework policy. While the CDFA supports telework where possible, in\-person attendance may be required based on operational needs. Employees are expected to be able to report to their worksite with minimal notification if an urgent need arises, as determined by the Department.

jobs.title: Service Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Job Summary:**

Under the direction of the Sales Manager and assigned Project Manager(s), this position is responsible for providing administrative support for the Service Sales Engineers, Project Management Team, and Plumbing Field Team.  



**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

Schedule and Route Optimization


The Project Coordinator acts as the dedicated bridge between Dispatch, the Field, and our Clients. Call centers and dispatch teams are built for speed, volume, and immediate routing; they get bogged down when forced to manage multi\-step, ongoing issues. This role takes ownership of those escalated, long\-term, or high\-tier requests, providing "white\-glove" oversight to ensure complex jobs are executed flawlessly from intake to completion.  

* 

Key Responsibilities


* Take ownership of escalated or complex service tickets handed off from Dispatch or PM’s.
* Serve as the dedicated, single point of contact for clients requiring multi\-step service or project fulfillment.
* Coordinate schedules, parts, resources, and communications between field technicians, internal departments, and third\-party vendors.
* Monitor ongoing project timelines to ensure longer\-term deliverables do not stall or fall through the cracks.
* Proactively update clients on the status of their service requests to eliminate inbound follow\-up calls to the dispatch team.
* Maintain accurate, detailed records of complex cases within the company’s CRM or project management software.
* Board Management: Constantly shifting the puzzle pieces throughout the day as jobs run long or finish early. A PC is always thinking two moves ahead.
* Skill Matching: Assigning complex jobs to senior technicians, while routing simpler tasks to junior techs.
* Equipment Assignment: Scheduling out equipment to techs for high level tracking.
Last Calls: Pushing to get last calls covered.  
* 

Call Triage and Customer Service


* Prevent Technicians from responding without necessary context: Technicians need enough information to mentally prepare for the diagnosis, grab the right tools out of the truck, and approach the customer with the right tone. Ask probing questions during the intake call helps set our technicians up for success while on site. "Plumbing leak" does not provide enough of a description to provide the proper level of service. Technicians need to know the location, severity, and context of the issue so they know what to expect. The Project Coordinator helps fill any gaps prior to arriving on site.
* Emergency Triage: Differentiate between a true emergency and a nuisance issue and prioritize the schedule accordingly.
* Setting Expectations: Communicating arrival windows clearly and sending "on the way" notifications so customers aren't left guessing.
* De\-escalation: Handling frustrated customers if a technician is running behind due to a previous job running long.
Empathy: Customer State of Mind\- (Urgency) Customer is frantic, water is actively destroying property. (Frustrating) Customer is annoyed, possible call back, invoice cost issue. Your role is to discern the situation and handle as a top priority for high level customer service.  
* 

Technician Support and Liaison


* Debriefing: Requiring techs to call or message in after every job to close out the ticket, ensure notes are accurate, and clear them for the next call.
* Logistical Support: Coordinating with parts supply houses if a tech needs a specific part or arranging for a junior tech to drop off a part to a senior tech on a big job.
* Gatekeeping: Making sure techs are on schedule and direct communication with techs and customers.
Safety tool box talk documentation and tracking.  
* 

Administrative and CRM Management


* Data Integrity: Ensuring all customer information is updated (new chief engineer,) property rules and regs, entry codes, and job histories are accurately entered into the CRM.
* Permit Coordination: Assisting with pulling municipal permits for major work like sewer replacements or gas line repairs.
* On Call Calendar: Assigning tech to the on call schedule and managing holiday fairness.
* Backflow Portal Administrator: Entering in all backflow forms on agency portals.
* Track Service Calls: Notify the PM of a service call. Communicate with tech for any follow\-up work or gaps to fill.
* Take and distribute meeting minutes for sales and department team meetings; email recap with action items to meeting attendees
* Assist with onboarding new hires – coordinate with Human Resource to ensure that all first day activities are scheduled in advance, itinerary, meet \& greets, etc.
* Assist the manager with new hire equipment setup; ITPAFs, business cards, key fob/building access, email setup, etc. to ensure a successful onboarding process.
* Prequalification Support for approved RFP's and bids.
* IFS and Bid Tracer Super User – Generating reports for the Sales Manager that tracks individual sales activity
* Monitor proposal and bid activity levels in the three main business segments (Retrofit, Repairs \& Maintenance)
* Scheduling of Estimate reviews with sales personnel and the Sales Managers.
* Scheduling of Pre\-job planning and Risk Review meetings – Scheduling required attendees based upon scope and dollar amount i.e., RVP, SVP etc..
* Plans and organizes meetings for Service leadership, Sales Managers, salespeople and vendors as needed by the Sales Manager including rooms and catering (for both in person and virtual meetings as applicable)
* General administrative duties such as typing and photocopying general correspondence including, but not limited to: letters, proposals, presentations, reports, agreements, contracts, and memos from notes or sending and/or distributing various correspondences on behalf of Project Managers
* Maintain accurate filing system and project document control.
* Take and transcribe meeting notes.
Other tasks and duties as assigned by Sales Managers, direct supervisor and/or upper management  
*

jobs.description:
Overview:

Do you want to build an impactful career to change the world for the better?


Geosyntec has an exciting opportunity for an **Experienced Environmental Scientist** **– Site Characterization, Remediation, and Emerging Contaminants** to join our Lakewood, Colorado office. This role is well aligned for an experienced scientist and technical leader with a strong background in contaminated site assessment, remediation, and emerging contaminants, including PFAS. The position will support complex environmental investigation and remediation projects for federal, industrial, municipal, public\-sector, and private\-sector clients, including site characterization, groundwater and soil assessment, source evaluation, remedial alternatives evaluations, remedial strategy development, and practical translation of technical findings into defensible site\-management approaches.  

Geosyntec is an innovative, international engineering and consulting firm serving private and public\-sector clients to address new ventures and complex problems involving our environment, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. Our engineers, scientists, technical and project employees serve our clients from offices across the world. Ranked by ENR as one of the top environmental engineering design firms, Geosyntec is internationally known for its technical leadership, broad experience, and exceptional client service.  

We invest in our people. Each employee is unique, and your career at Geosyntec will be too. We offer competitive pay and benefits, and well\-being programs to support you and your family.  

To Learn More Visit: http://www.geosyntec.com/careers/.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
* Provide technical leadership for contaminated site assessment, remediation, applied research, fate\-and\-transport evaluations, and remedial decision support for federal, industrial, municipal, public\-sector, and private\-sector clients, including projects involving PFAS and other emerging contaminants.
* Lead and support site characterization and remedial alternatives evaluations , including source\-area delineation, contaminant distribution, groundwater and soil assessment, migration pathway evaluations, and remedial strategy development for PFAS and non\-PFAS contaminants.
* Develop, refine, and communicate high\-resolution and three\-dimensional conceptual site models integrating hydrogeologic, geochemical, analytical, statistical, and modeling results to support adaptive investigation strategies and defensible remedial decisions.
* Plan, coordinate, and technically oversee investigation activities involving soil, groundwater, sediment, surface water, porewater, soil stockpiles, vadose\-zone media, and other impacted matrices while maintaining a strong focus on health, safety, quality, and data defensibility.
* Prepare, review, and manage technical deliverables, including work plans, quality assurance plans/sampling and analysis plans, conceptual site model products, technical memoranda, treatability evaluations, decision\-support materials, proposals, presentations, and regulatory or client briefing materials.
* Coordinate with clients, federal and state regulatory agencies, installation stakeholders, subcontractors, academic collaborators, technical experts, and internal teams to support regulatory engagement, technical alignment, and successful project delivery.
* Support proposal development, client development, technical marketing, and research\-to\-practice initiatives related to contaminated site assessment, remediation, emerging contaminants, treatment, source evaluation, and remedial decision support.
* Mentor early and mid\-career staff in environmental data analysis, conceptual site model development, technical interpretation, and clear communication of complex scientific results.
* Drive personal, company, and rental vehicles to client or company project or office sites, and other business locations, as needed.


Education and Licensure:
* Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, geology, environmental engineering, civil engineering, chemistry, biology, natural resources science, or a closely related field. (required)
* Advanced degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, civil engineering, hydrogeology, geochemistry, biogeochemistry, or a closely related technical discipline. (preferred)


Skills, Experience and Qualifications:
* At least 7 years of experience (8\+ years preferred) in environmental consulting, applied research, remediation, contaminated site assessment, site characterization, or federal environmental programs, with experience involving PFAS, emerging contaminants, or other regulated contaminants; or equivalent combination of education and experience. (required)
* Demonstrated experience leading or providing technical support for environmental investigations, contaminant fate\-and\-transport analyses, remedial alternatives evaluations, site restoration programs, or remediation projects for federal, industrial, municipal, public\-sector, and private\-sector clients. (preferred)
* Experience preparing, reviewing, and managing technical documents such as work plans, technical memoranda, reports, conceptual site model summaries, remedial alternatives evaluations, and decision\-support products. (preferred)
* Experience managing multidisciplinary technical teams, scopes, budgets, schedules, subcontractors, task orders, proposal efforts, technical QA/QC, and multiple concurrent consulting or research assignments. (required)
* Experience with environmental data analysis and visualization tools used to interpret complex environmental datasets, including statistical analysis, spatial visualization, hydrogeologic interpretation, maps, tables, figures, and client\-ready graphics. (preferred)

**About the engagement**  
A state regulatory agency needs a spatial analysis of licensed delivery operations in a regulated market: where delivery service exists, where it does not, and which populations sit outside any current service area. The agency will use the resulting map to evaluate service area expansion requests and to identify underserved geography. The product becomes a standing tool the agency maintains after the engagement ends.

**What you would do**

* Geocode and validate licensed operator and delivery asset location data provided by the client
* Build service area layers using defensible assumptions, including drive\-time isochrones rather than simple radius buffers
* Overlay coverage against population, density, and relevant demographic geography to identify and quantify service gaps
* Produce an interactive web map that agency staff can use without desktop GIS software or a paid license
* Produce static, print\-quality map exhibits suitable for a report submitted to a state legislature
* Document data sources, projections, service area assumptions, and update procedures so agency staff can refresh the map in future cycles
* Deliver clean project files and layers in a format the client retains

**Required**

* Three or more years of applied GIS work with a portfolio of finished maps
* Proficiency with ArcGIS Pro or QGIS, and comfort producing web\-deliverable output (ArcGIS Online, Leaflet, Mapbox, Felt, or comparable)
* Geocoding and address validation experience with messy administrative data
* Network or drive\-time service area analysis experience
* Strong cartographic judgment. Output will be read by policymakers, not analysts
* Ability to document methods clearly enough for someone else to reproduce them
* Availability to deliver against fixed dates in November and December

**Preferred**

* Bachelor's or master's in geography, GIS, urban planning, public health, or a related field
* Experience with public sector or regulatory clients
* Python scripting for geoprocessing automation
* Experience with accessibility or service coverage analysis in any sector, including health care, transit, food access, or broadband

Expected hours: 35\.0 per week

Work Location: Remote

Overview:

Do you want to build an impactful career to change the world for the better?


Geosyntec has an exciting opportunity for an **Experienced Environmental Scientist** **– Site Characterization, Remediation, and Emerging Contaminants** to join our Lakewood, Colorado office. This role is well aligned for an experienced scientist and technical leader with a strong background in contaminated site assessment, remediation, and emerging contaminants, including PFAS. The position will support complex environmental investigation and remediation projects for federal, industrial, municipal, public\-sector, and private\-sector clients, including site characterization, groundwater and soil assessment, source evaluation, remedial alternatives evaluations, remedial strategy development, and practical translation of technical findings into defensible site\-management approaches.  

Geosyntec is an innovative, international engineering and consulting firm serving private and public\-sector clients to address new ventures and complex problems involving our environment, natural resources, and civil infrastructure. Our engineers, scientists, technical and project employees serve our clients from offices across the world. Ranked by ENR as one of the top environmental engineering design firms, Geosyntec is internationally known for its technical leadership, broad experience, and exceptional client service.  

We invest in our people. Each employee is unique, and your career at Geosyntec will be too. We offer competitive pay and benefits, and well\-being programs to support you and your family.  

To Learn More Visit: http://www.geosyntec.com/careers/.

* Coordinate with clients, federal and state regulatory agencies, installation stakeholders, subcontractors, academic collaborators, technical experts, and internal teams to support regulatory engagement, technical alignment, and successful project delivery.

(required)

(preferred)
* Experience preparing, reviewing, and managing technical documents such as work plans, technical memoranda, reports, conceptual site model summaries, remedial alternatives evaluations, and decision\-support products. (preferred)
* Experience managing multidisciplinary technical teams, scopes, budgets, schedules, subcontractors, task orders, proposal efforts, technical QA/QC, and multiple concurrent consulting or research assignments. (required)
* Experience with environmental data analysis and visualization tools used to interpret complex environmental datasets, including statistical analysis, spatial visualization, hydrogeologic interpretation, maps, tables, figures, and client\-ready graphics. (preferred)
